prerequisites: Students should have a solid grasp of basic programming knowledge from the first semester, especially variables, control structures, functions, and simple data structures like arrays.
A basic understanding of mathematical concepts such as sets, simple logic, sums, and growth rates is also important, as these are needed for algorithm analysis.
First experiences with systematic problem-solving and structured development of small programs are helpful.
Familiarity with development environments and the willingness to think abstractly and analytically support a successful start in the module.

learning_outcomes.text: Students gain a comprehensive overview of the fundamentals of algorithms and data structures, including the concept of algorithms, the importance of efficiency and complexity in algorithm analysis, and an overview of elementary data structures such as lists, sets, trees, and hash tables.
Students know important algorithms and data structures as well as techniques for analyzing their complexity.
Students can distinguish algorithms based on their quality and select, explain, and implement suitable algorithms and data structures for simple applications in context.
Students focus on a deep understanding of the properties, analysis, and application of algorithms and data structures, as well as their interaction.
They learn how algorithms for searching and sorting work and engage with methods of algorithm design and selected algorithms on graphs.
Students reflect on and evaluate the epistemic validity of factual statements in the field of algorithms and data structures based on the situation.
They are able to apply this knowledge in the context of real and complex problems, critically question it, and weigh different approaches against each other.

Through this profound understanding, they can develop innovative solution approaches based on plausible factual considerations, thereby contributing to the solution of practical and theoretical problems in computer science and related disciplines.
Students should be able to use algorithms and data structures to solve real-world problems.
This includes the ability to select suitable data structures for specific applications and to design and implement algorithms accordingly.
Students learn to communicate their ideas and solutions effectively within the team.
They work together to solve complex problems and learn from each other.
Students gain an awareness of the ethical and societal implications of computer science.
They reflect on the responsibility associated with the development and application of algorithms, especially regarding data protection, fairness, and transparency.

syllabus_topics: Elementary Data Structures (e.g., Lists, Sets, Trees, Hashing)
teaching_methods: Supervised small group work (in-person or online)
assessment_rules: Graded assessment can be an exam, a multiple-choice exam, or a combination of both; the duration is defined by the respective valid study regulations. Ungraded assessment includes experimental work (approx. 3 experiments) or practical work samples (approx. 3 assignments).
bibliography: T. H. Cormen, C. E. Leiserson, R. Rivest und C. Stein, Algorithmen - Eine Einführung, München: Oldenbourg, jeweils aktuelle Auflage
